components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
犭 (dog, animal) — animals, as in 狗, 猫, 猪: a wild animal.
王 (wáng) is a loose sound clue for kuáng; 王 also in 往 wǎng and 旺 wàng.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,她几乎要发狂了。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā jīhū yào fākuángle.
example.english: Hearing this news, she nearly went crazy.
example.fact: The 1518 Strasbourg dancing plague saw dozens of people reportedly dance uncontrollably in the streets for days, some until they collapsed from exhaustion — historians now suspect it was a case of mass psychogenic illness driven by extreme stress rather than any physical disease.

examples.hanzi: 孩子不见了，妈妈急得发狂。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bú jiàn le, māma jí de fākuáng.
examples.english: The child was missing and the mother was frantic.

examples.hanzi: 看到比分，球迷们高兴得发狂。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào bǐfēn, qiúmímen gāoxìng de fākuáng.
examples.english: Seeing the score, the fans went wild with joy.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 士兵们挖了一条地道逃出了监狱。
example.pinyin: Shìbīngmen wāle yī tiáo dìdào táochūle jiānyù.
example.english: The soldiers dug a tunnel and escaped from the prison.
example.fact: The Channel Tunnel connecting England and France runs 50 kilometers under the English Channel, of which 37 kilometers are undersea — making it the tunnel with the longest undersea section in the world.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市有一个很长的地下地道。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu yí gè hěn cháng de dìxià dìdào.
examples.english: This city has a very long underground tunnel.

examples.hanzi: 他说一口地道的北京话。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō yì kǒu dìdao de Běijīnghuà.
examples.english: He speaks authentic Beijing dialect.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.

example.hanzi: 老师把学生分成了四个小组。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ xuésheng fēnchéngle sì gè xiǎozǔ.
example.english: The teacher divided the students into four groups.
example.fact: A single fertilized human egg divides roughly 40 times over about nine months of gestation to become the trillions of cells that make up a newborn baby.

examples.hanzi: 把蛋糕分成八块，大家都能吃到。
examples.pinyin: Bǎ dàngāo fēnchéng bā kuài, dàjiā dōu néng chīdào.
examples.english: Divide the cake into eight pieces so everyone gets some.

examples.hanzi: 这本书分成上下两册。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū fēnchéng shàng xià liǎng cè.
examples.english: This book is divided into two volumes.

components.note: 尸 (body) — the top part: a person. Dictionary: a man measuring by pacing; with the stroke below it, the stride or a ruler.
乚 (hook) — the bottom stroke, the measuring step. Memory aid: a foot-length ruler, as in 英尺 foot (unit).
寸 (inch) — a hand with a dot marking the pulse about an inch from the wrist; as a part it appears in 对, 寻, 守, 村.

example.hanzi: 请告诉我这件衣服的尺寸。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ zhè jiàn yīfu de chǐcun.
example.english: Please tell me the size of this piece of clothing.
example.fact: The international standard meter was defined in 1799 as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator; today it's defined instead by the distance light travels in a fraction of a second, a definition precise enough to be reproduced in any laboratory on Earth.

examples.hanzi: 这双鞋的尺寸有点小。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié de chǐcùn yǒudiǎn xiǎo.
examples.english: The size of these shoes is a little small.

examples.hanzi: 你要量一下窗户的尺寸，再买窗帘。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào liáng yíxià chuānghu de chǐcùn, zài mǎi chuānglián.
examples.english: You should measure the window dimensions before buying curtains.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 车 is a cart or vehicle, as in 轮, 输, 车; 转 is turning of wheels.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 转 is zhuǎn; 专 also sounds out 传 chuán and 砖 zhuān.
向 (toward) — a window 口 in a wall facing a direction, hence toward. It also gives its sound to 响 xiǎng and 饷 xiǎng.

example.hanzi: 汽车突然转向,躲开了路上的障碍物。
example.pinyin: Qìchē tūrán zhuǎnxiàng, duǒkāile lù shàng de zhàng'àiwù.
example.english: The car suddenly changed direction to avoid the obstacle on the road.
example.fact: Modern car power steering systems can reduce the physical effort needed to turn the wheel by up to 80%, using hydraulic or electric assistance — a far cry from early automobiles, which sometimes required a driver's full upper-body strength to steer at low speed.

examples.hanzi: 前面有路障，司机赶紧转向。
examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn yǒu lùzhàng, sījī gǎnjǐn zhuǎnxiàng.
examples.english: There was a roadblock ahead, and the driver swerved quickly.

examples.hanzi: 风向转向了，天气要变冷了。
examples.pinyin: Fēngxiàng zhuǎnxiàng le, tiānqì yào biàn lěng le.
examples.english: The wind has changed direction, so it's going to get colder.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 他大部分时间都待在家中。
example.pinyin: Tā dàbùfen shíjiān dōu dāizài jiāzhōng.
example.english: He spends most of his time at home.
example.fact: Studies of pre-industrial societies suggest people historically spent far more of their waking hours performing labor at or near their dwelling than modern urban office workers do — the sharp separation between 'home' and 'workplace' is largely a product of the last two centuries of industrialization.

examples.hanzi: 他把家中的旧书送给了图书馆。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ jiāzhōng de jiù shū sòng gěi le túshūguǎn.
examples.english: He donated the old books from his home to the library.

examples.hanzi: 家中一切都好，请不要挂念。
examples.pinyin: Jiāzhōng yíqiè dōu hǎo, qǐng búyào guàniàn.
examples.english: Everything is fine at home, so please don't worry.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — striking or acting: 教, 放, 政; 敌 is an opponent to strike.
舌 here is a form of 啇 (dí), the sound part; also in 滴 dī and 嫡 dí.

example.hanzi: 这支球队本赛季几乎无敌。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì běn sàijì jīhū wúdí.
example.english: This team has been nearly unbeatable this season.
example.fact: The Boston Celtics' 1985–86 NBA season included a 40–1 home record, one of the most dominant home-court performances in league history and a mark still cited as a benchmark for near invincibility.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏里的英雄是无敌的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì lǐ de yīngxióng shì wúdí de.
examples.english: The hero in this game is invincible.

examples.hanzi: 孩子觉得爸爸在他心中是无敌的。
examples.pinyin: Háizi juéde bàba zài tā xīnzhōng shì wúdí de.
examples.english: The child thinks his dad is invincible.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.

example.hanzi: 请把合同用传真发给我们。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ hétong yòng chuánzhēn fāgěi wǒmen.
example.english: Please fax us the contract.
example.fact: The fax machine is far older than most people assume — Scottish inventor Alexander Bain patented an early fax-like device in 1843, decades before the telephone, using a pendulum-based scanning mechanism to transmit images over telegraph wires.

examples.hanzi: 这份文件我已经传真给你了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn wénjiàn wǒ yǐjīng chuánzhēn gěi nǐ le.
examples.english: I've already faxed this document to you.

examples.hanzi: 我们办公室还有一台传真机。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bàngōngshì hái yǒu yì tái chuánzhēnjī.
examples.english: Our office still has a fax machine.

meanings: (of a relationship etc) to break down

components.note: 石 (stone) — stones and hard things: 研, 码, 砖; 破 is to smash or break.
皮 (pí) is a loose sound clue; same series 坡 pō, 披 pī, 波 bō.
衣 (clothing) — cloth ripping apart; also as 衤 in 衬, 被.
列 (liè) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 烈 liè.

example.hanzi: 谈判在最后一刻破裂了。
example.pinyin: Tánpàn zài zuìhòu yī kè pòlièle.
example.english: The negotiations broke down at the last moment.
example.fact: The 1963 Vajont Dam disaster in Italy occurred not because the dam itself failed, but because a massive landslide into the reservoir sent a wave over the top of the dam — a reminder that structural failure in large infrastructure can come from the surrounding geology rather than the structure itself.

examples.hanzi: 一场大雨后，水管破裂了。
examples.pinyin: Yì chǎng dàyǔ hòu, shuǐguǎn pòliè le.
examples.english: After a heavy rain, the water pipe burst.

examples.hanzi: 他们的婚姻已经破裂了。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de hūnyīn yǐjīng pòliè le.
examples.english: Their marriage has fallen apart.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — marks hearing and the ear, as in 聪 clever, 听 listen; 聋 is deaf.
龙 (lóng) — same sound: 聋 lóng. 龙 also sounds out 笼 lóng and 咙 lóng.

example.hanzi: 他的爷爷耳朵聋了。
example.pinyin: Tā de yéye ěrduo lóng le.
example.english: His grandfather has gone deaf.
example.fact: 聋 gives 聋哑 (deaf and mute) and 装聋作哑 ('pretend to be deaf and dumb'), meaning to feign ignorance.

examples.hanzi: 他的耳朵有点聋，说话要大声一点。
examples.pinyin: Tā de ěrduo yǒudiǎn lóng, shuōhuà yào dàshēng yìdiǎn.
examples.english: He is a bit hard of hearing, so speak up.

examples.hanzi: 这个学校有聋哑学生。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xuéxiào yǒu lóngyǎ xuésheng.
examples.english: This school has deaf and mute students.

components.note: 广 (a roof on a wall) — buildings and rooms: 店 shop, 床 bed, 库 store, 度. Here also the simplified form of 廣, broad.

example.hanzi: 他的知识面很广。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhīshi miàn hěn guǎng.
example.english: He has wide-ranging knowledge.
example.fact: As a word, 广 (simplified from 廣) means wide: 广告 (advert), 广场 (square), 广泛 (widespread) and 广东 (Guangdong). As a character part, 广 is the 'cliff-house' radical read yǎn.

examples.hanzi: 这家商店的商品种类很广。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn de shāngpǐn zhǒnglèi hěn guǎng.
examples.english: This store has a wide range of goods.

examples.hanzi: 他在电视上看到了一个广告。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài diànshì shàng kàndào le yí ge guǎnggào.
examples.english: He saw an advertisement on TV.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — marks clothes and wrapping, as in 衬, 装, 袋; in 裹 the 衣 literally wraps around 果.
果 (guǒ) gives the sound exactly: 裹 guǒ.

example.hanzi: 她用毯子把孩子裹起来。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng tǎnzi bǎ háizi guǒ qǐlái.
example.english: She wrapped the child in a blanket.
example.fact: 裹 is in 包裹 (parcel), 裹挟 (to sweep along), 裹足不前 (hold back) and 裹腹 (to fill the stomach).

examples.hanzi: 冬天我们裹着大衣出门。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān wǒmen guǒ zhe dàyī chūmén.
examples.english: In winter we go out wrapped in big coats.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈把饺子裹得很好看。
examples.pinyin: Māma bǎ jiǎozi guǒ de hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: Mom wraps the dumplings so they look pretty.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their roles, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 信 trust; 储 is a person laying something by, to store, as in 储蓄 savings.
诸 (zhū) — loose sound hint (chǔ vs zhū); same part in 煮 zhǔ and 著 zhù.

example.hanzi: 我每个月都储一点钱。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měi gè yuè dōu chǔ yìdiǎn qián.
example.english: I save a bit of money every month.
example.fact: 储 is a bound form: 储蓄 (savings), 储存 (store), 储备 (reserve), 存储 (storage) and 储物柜 (locker).

examples.hanzi: 他每个月都储蓄一部分工资。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi ge yuè dōu chǔxù yí bùfen gōngzī.
examples.english: Every month he saves part of his salary.

examples.hanzi: 我的手机储存空间不够了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī chǔcún kōngjiān bú gòu le.
examples.english: My phone is running out of storage space.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢.
周 (zhōu) is a loose sound clue for diào/tiáo; 周 also in 凋 diāo.

example.hanzi: 医生强调了充足睡眠的重要性。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng qiángdiàole chōngzú shuìmián de zhòngyàoxìng.
example.english: The doctor emphasized the importance of adequate sleep.
example.fact: The American researcher Randy Gardner's famous 1964 stint of staying awake for about 264 hours remains one of the most studied cases of extreme sleep deprivation on record, and it's part of why researchers now strongly discourage attempting to break such records.

examples.hanzi: 老师特别强调了这一点。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī tèbié qiángdiào le zhè yì diǎn.
examples.english: The teacher put special emphasis on this point.

examples.hanzi: 他一再强调，安全第一。
examples.pinyin: Tā yízài qiángdiào, ānquán dì-yī.
examples.english: He repeatedly stressed that safety comes first.

meanings: (painting, embroidery etc) without following a model
(abbr. for 空手道[kong1 shou3 dao4]) karate

components.note: 穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 他空手夺下了对方的匕首。
example.pinyin: Tā kōngshǒu duóxiàle duìfāng de bǐshǒu.
example.english: He disarmed the opponent's dagger with his bare hands.
example.fact: Karate developed on the Ryukyu Islands, particularly Okinawa, partly as a response to a centuries-long ban on carrying weapons imposed by ruling authorities — practitioners trained empty-handed combat techniques that could be disguised within ordinary agricultural tool movements.

examples.hanzi: 他是空手来的，什么也没带。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì kōngshǒu lái de, shénme yě méi dài.
examples.english: He came empty-handed, bringing nothing.

examples.hanzi: 空手去别人家拜访不太礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Kōngshǒu qù biérén jiā bàifǎng bú tài lǐmào.
examples.english: It's not very polite to visit someone's home empty-handed.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — oldest form: a person bending over a basin of water to see a reflection; 鉴 jiàn (mirror) adds metal. To look closely, to supervise.
口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.

example.hanzi: 政府部门被指控监听公民的电话。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ bùmén bèi zhǐkòng jiāntīng gōngmín de diànhuà.
example.english: The government department was accused of wiretapping citizens' phone calls.
example.fact: The 1972 Watergate break-in, in which operatives tied to President Nixon's re-election campaign attempted to wiretap the Democratic National Committee's offices, is one of the most consequential eavesdropping operations in American political history.

examples.hanzi: 他怀疑有人在监听他的电话。
examples.pinyin: Tā huáiyí yǒu rén zài jiāntīng tā de diànhuà.
examples.english: He suspects someone is wiretapping his phone.

examples.hanzi: 这个软件会偷偷监听你的声音。
examples.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn huì tōutōu jiāntīng nǐ de shēngyīn.
examples.english: This software secretly listens to your voice.

components.note: 两 (liǎng) — two, a pair; as a part it sounds out 辆 liàng and 俩 liǎ.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.hanzi: 街道两边种满了樱花树。
example.pinyin: Jiēdào liǎngbiān zhòngmǎnle yīnghuā shù.
example.english: Both sides of the street were lined with cherry blossom trees.
example.fact: Washington, D.C.'s famous cherry trees, planted along the Tidal Basin starting in 1912, were a gift from the city of Tokyo, and the annual bloom now draws over a million visitors each spring to see roughly 3,800 trees flower for just one to two weeks.

examples.hanzi: 桌子两边各坐着两个人。
examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi liǎngbiān gè zuò zhe liǎng gè rén.
examples.english: Two people sit on each side of the table.

examples.hanzi: 过马路时，请先看清两边的车。
examples.pinyin: Guò mǎlù shí, qǐng xiān kànqīng liǎngbiān de chē.
examples.english: When crossing the road, first look at the cars on both sides.

components.note: 将 (jiāng) is the trimmed top part: 奖 jiǎng sounds like 桨 jiǎng and 浆 jiāng.
木 (wood) — 木 is wood — cups were first made of wood, as in 桌, 板, 树.
不 (bù) — loose hint — 杯 is bēi; 不 shares just the b- start.

example.hanzi: 冠军队举起了金色的奖杯。
example.pinyin: Guànjūn duì jǔqǐle jīnsè de jiǎngbēi.
example.english: The champion team lifted the golden trophy.
example.fact: The FIFA World Cup trophy, awarded since 1974, is made of 18-karat gold and weighs about 6.1 kilograms — winning teams don't actually keep the original trophy but receive a gold-plated replica instead, since the real one is returned to FIFA after the ceremony.

examples.hanzi: 他在比赛中拿到了一座奖杯。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng nádào le yí zuò jiǎngbēi.
examples.english: He won a trophy in the competition.

examples.hanzi: 这个奖杯是用银做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiǎngbēi shì yòng yín zuò de.
examples.english: This trophy is made of silver.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.
夕 (evening, night) — night and time: 外, 多, 夜; dreams come at night, so 夕 is the meaning clue; 林 is only filler.

example.hanzi: 祝你今晚做个美梦。
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ jīnwǎn zuò gè měimèng.
example.english: I wish you a beautiful dream tonight.
example.fact: Most vivid dreaming occurs during REM sleep, a stage the body enters roughly every 90 minutes throughout the night — during REM, the brain becomes almost as active as when awake, even though most voluntary muscles are temporarily paralyzed, a state that likely prevents sleepers from acting out their dreams.

examples.hanzi: 昨晚我做了一个美梦。
examples.pinyin: Zuówǎn wǒ zuò le yí gè měimèng.
examples.english: Last night I had a lovely dream.

examples.hanzi: 别打扰他，他正在做美梦呢。
examples.pinyin: Bié dǎrǎo tā, tā zhèngzài zuò měimèng ne.
examples.english: Don't disturb him; he is having a sweet dream.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 激 is water surging up, then to stir up.
敫 (jiǎo) is only a loose sound clue for jī.
氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤; water means life: 活 is alive.
舌 (shé, tongue) is a loose sound clue for huó; also in 话 huà.

example.hanzi: 这个软件需要输入激活码才能激活。
example.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn xūyào shūrù jīhuómǎ cáinéng jīhuó.
example.english: This software requires entering an activation code to be activated.
example.fact: In 1889, the Swedish chemist Svante Arrhenius proposed that every chemical reaction needs a minimum burst of energy — activation energy — to get started, even reactions that release energy overall. The equation he derived, still called the Arrhenius equation, lets chemists calculate how fast a reaction proceeds at a given temperature. It is part of why refrigeration slows spoilage: colder molecules have less kinetic energy available to clear that activation barrier.

examples.hanzi: 我的手机卡还没有激活。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī kǎ hái méiyǒu jīhuó.
examples.english: My phone SIM card hasn't been activated yet.

examples.hanzi: 运动可以激活大脑，让人更有精神。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng kěyǐ jīhuó dànǎo, ràng rén gèng yǒu jīngshen.
examples.english: Exercise can activate the brain and make people more energetic.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — a body-part radical, as in 脸 face, 脚 foot, 胖 fat; 肿 is flesh swelling.
中 (zhōng) gives a close sound, with a different tone; 种 zhǒng shares the same pair.

example.hanzi: 他的脚肿了。
example.pinyin: Tā de jiǎo zhǒng le.
example.english: His foot is swollen.
example.fact: 肿 gives 肿瘤 (tumour), 浮肿 (puffiness), 红肿 (red and swollen) and 肿胀.

examples.hanzi: 他被蚊子咬了，脸都肿了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi wénzi yǎo le, liǎn dōu zhǒng le.
examples.english: He was bitten by a mosquito and his face swelled up.

examples.hanzi: 我的手指肿得很厉害。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒuzhǐ zhǒng de hěn lìhai.
examples.english: My finger is badly swollen.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, from 肉) — marks body parts, as in 肚 belly, 脸 face, 腿 leg; 膜 is a membrane, a thin layer of tissue.
莫 (mò) — same sound: 膜 mó. 莫 also sounds out 摸 mō and 幕 mù.

example.hanzi: 我用面膜护肤。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yòng miànmó hùfū.
example.english: I use a face mask for skincare.
example.fact: 膜 gives 面膜 (face mask), 薄膜 (thin film), 耳膜 (eardrum), 视网膜 (retina) and 保鲜膜 (cling film). 膜拜 now also means to adore someone.

examples.hanzi: 这张贴膜要小心贴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng tiēmó yào xiǎoxīn tiē.
examples.english: You need to apply this screen protector carefully.

examples.hanzi: 眼睛里有一层薄薄的膜。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnjing lǐ yǒu yì céng báobáo de mó.
examples.english: There is a thin membrane in the eye.

components.note: 舌 (tongue) — 舌 is the tongue, as in 话, 活; 辞 is words and speech, and the same sound as 词 cí.

example.hanzi: 他辞职了。
example.pinyin: Tā cízhí le.
example.english: He resigned.
example.fact: 辞 is formal: 辞职 (resign), 辞退 (dismiss), 告辞 (take leave), 辞典 (dictionary), 不辞而别 (leave without saying goodbye). Compare 词 (word).

examples.hanzi: 他向公司提出了辞职。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng gōngsī tíchū le cízhí.
examples.english: He handed in his resignation to the company.

examples.hanzi: 我想向各位告辞了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xiàng gèwèi gàocí le.
examples.english: I would like to take my leave of everyone.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — marks bows and stretching, as in 张 stretch, 引 draw; 弘 is expanding, like a bow drawn wide.

example.hanzi: 他想弘扬中国文化。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng hóngyáng Zhōngguó wénhuà.
example.english: He wants to promote Chinese culture.
example.fact: 弘 is formal: 弘扬 (promote), 弘大 (grand). It is interchangeable with 宏 in some words, and appears in names such as 弘一法师.

examples.hanzi: 他想弘扬传统文化。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng hóngyáng chuántǒng wénhuà.
examples.english: He wants to promote traditional culture.

examples.hanzi: 我们要弘扬勤劳的好传统。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào hóngyáng qínláo de hǎo chuántǒng.
examples.english: We should carry forward the good tradition of hard work.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — marks birds, as in 鸡 chicken, 鸭 duck; 鹅 is the goose, as in 企鹅 penguin.
我 (wǒ) — only a loose sound hint (é vs wǒ); same part in 俄 é and 饿 è.

example.hanzi: 河边有几只白鹅。
example.pinyin: Hébiān yǒu jǐ zhī bái é.
example.english: There are a few white geese by the river.
example.fact: The measure word is 只. 鹅 is the subject of the famous children's poem 《咏鹅》 'é, é, é', traditionally attributed to Luo Binwang at the age of seven.

examples.hanzi: 农场里养着一群大白鹅。
examples.pinyin: Nóngchǎng lǐ yǎng zhe yì qún dà báié.
examples.english: The farm keeps a flock of big white geese.

examples.hanzi: 鹅喜欢在池塘里游泳。
examples.pinyin: É xǐhuan zài chítáng lǐ yóuyǒng.
examples.english: Geese like to swim in the pond.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 胸 is the chest.
匈 (xiōng) gives the sound exactly: 胸 xiōng.
罒 (net, 网 variant) — marks nets and covers, as in 罗, 罚; 罩 is a cover or a basket net, as in 胸罩 bra.
卓 (zhuó) — only a loose sound hint (zhào vs zhuó).

example.hanzi: 她在商场里买了一件新胸罩。
example.pinyin: Tā zài shāngchǎng lǐ mǎile yí jiàn xīn xiōngzhào.
example.english: She bought a new bra at the mall.
example.fact: The modern brassiere traces to a 1914 US patent by socialite Mary Phelps Jacob, who fashioned one from two silk handkerchiefs and a ribbon as a lighter alternative to the rigid, whalebone-boned corsets then in fashion. She later sold the patent to the Warner Brothers Corset Company for $1,500, a sum worth over $40,000 today. Within a few decades the corset industry itself had largely been displaced by the garment she improvised.

examples.hanzi: 这件胸罩的尺寸有点小。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn xiōngzhào de chǐcùn yǒudiǎn xiǎo.
examples.english: This bra is a little small in size.

examples.hanzi: 她在网上给自己买了两件运动胸罩。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǎngshàng gěi zìjǐ mǎi le liǎng jiàn yùndòng xiōngzhào.
examples.english: She bought two sports bras for herself online.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 优 first meant a person who performs or is excellent, in 演员 and 优秀.
尤 (yóu) — near sound — 优 is yōu; 尤 also sounds out 忧 yōu.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 每个人都有自己的优点和缺点。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de yōudiǎn hé quēdiǎn.
example.english: Everyone has their own strengths and weaknesses.
example.fact: The economist David Ricardo argued in 1817 that a country benefits from trade by focusing on what it produces with the smallest relative sacrifice, even if a trading partner is better at making everything outright — a principle he called comparative advantage. It remains one of the few ideas in economics that most professional economists agree on, and it still underpins arguments for international trade today.

examples.hanzi: 这个手机的最大优点是电池耐用。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒujī de zuì dà yōudiǎn shì diànchí nàiyòng.
examples.english: The biggest advantage of this phone is its durable battery.

examples.hanzi: 他的优点是做事认真。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yōudiǎn shì zuòshì rènzhēn.
examples.english: His strength is that he works carefully.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 谢谢你的好意，但我现在不需要帮助。
example.pinyin: Xièxiè nǐ de hǎoyì, dàn wǒ xiànzài bù xūyào bāngzhù.
example.english: Thank you for your kindness, but I don't need help right now.
example.fact: Vampire bats that fail to find blood on a given night are sometimes fed by roost-mates who regurgitate part of their own meal for them, a behavior first documented in detail by biologist Gerald Wilkinson in the 1980s. Bats that share food tend to be shared with in return later, and individuals that never reciprocate are eventually cut off — a rare, well-studied case of reciprocal generosity among mammals.

examples.hanzi: 他是一番好意，你别误会。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yì fān hǎoyì, nǐ bié wùhuì.
examples.english: He meant well, so don't get the wrong idea.

examples.hanzi: 我是出于好意才提醒你的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì chūyú hǎoyì cái tíxǐng nǐ de.
examples.english: I only reminded you out of good intentions.

components.note: 穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢.
周 (zhōu) is a loose sound clue for diào/tiáo; 周 also in 凋 diāo.

example.hanzi: 夏天没有空调真是太难受了。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān méiyǒu kōngtiáo zhēnshi tài nánshòu le.
example.english: Summer without air conditioning is really unbearable.
example.fact: Willis Carrier built the first modern electrical air conditioner in 1902, not to cool people but to control humidity at a Brooklyn printing plant, where damp air was making paper swell and ink misalign. Cooling the room was almost a side effect of controlling moisture. The technology later reshaped where large populations could comfortably live, from Phoenix to Dubai.

examples.hanzi: 这个房间的空调坏了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān de kōngtiáo huài le.
examples.english: The air conditioner in this room is broken.

examples.hanzi: 请把空调开到二十六度。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ kōngtiáo kāi dào èrshíliù dù.
examples.english: Please set the air conditioner to twenty-six degrees.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.
口 (mouth) — speaking, shouting: 叫, 吗, 喊; 号 is to call out, then a call-sign or number.
丂 (kǎo) is only a loose clue; it also appears in 考 kǎo and 巧 qiǎo.

example.hanzi: 他在书上做了一个记号，方便以后查找。
example.pinyin: Tā zài shū shàng zuòle yí gè jìhao, fāngbiàn yǐhòu cházhǎo.
example.english: He made a mark in the book to make it easier to find later.
example.fact: Long-distance hikers on the Appalachian Trail follow a marking system of white rectangular paint blazes on trees and rocks, a practice dating to the trail's early maintenance in the 1930s. The blazes are spaced closely enough that a hiker should always be able to spot the next one before losing sight of the last, letting the 3,500-kilometer trail be followed without a single continuous map.

examples.hanzi: 请在要记住的地方做个记号。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài yào jìzhù de dìfang zuò gè jìhào.
examples.english: Please make a mark where you need to remember.

examples.hanzi: 我在地图上画了一个红色的记号。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài dìtú shàng huà le yí gè hóngsè de jìhào.
examples.english: I drew a red mark on the map.

components.note: 讠 (speech; traditional 言) — marks speaking and language, as in 说 say, 话 speech, 谎 lie; 诈 is cheating by words.
乍 (zhà) — same sound: 诈 zhà. 乍 also sounds out 炸 zhà and 榨 zhà.
马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑 ride, 驾; 骗 first meant to jump on a horse.
扁 (biǎn) — near sound — 骗 is piàn; 扁 also sounds out 偏 piān, 篇 piān and 遍 biàn.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了那个诈骗团伙的头目。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔle nàge zhàpiàn tuánhuǒ de tóumù.
example.english: Police arrested the leader of that fraud ring.
example.fact: In 1920, Charles Ponzi promised investors 50% returns within 45 days by claiming to arbitrage international postal reply coupons. He paid early investors with money collected from new ones, and the scheme collapsed within months once withdrawals outpaced new deposits. His name became permanently attached to any fraud that pays existing investors with money from new ones rather than real profit.

examples.hanzi: 老人被骗子诈骗了一万块钱。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén bèi piànzi zhàpiàn le yíwàn kuài qián.
examples.english: The old man was swindled out of ten thousand yuan by a con artist.

examples.hanzi: 手机上经常收到诈骗短信。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī shàng jīngcháng shōudào zhàpiàn duǎnxìn.
examples.english: I often receive scam text messages on my phone.

components.note: 日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.
非 (not) — two wings spread in opposite directions, so "opposed, not". Gives sound to 啡 fēi, 排 pái and 悲 bēi.

example.hanzi: 这件事的是非曲直，还需要进一步调查。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì de shìfēi qūzhí, hái xūyào jìnyíbù diàochá.
example.english: The rights and wrongs of this matter still need further investigation.
example.fact: Philosopher Philippa Foot introduced the trolley problem in 1967, asking whether it is right to divert a runaway trolley so it kills one person instead of five. The thought experiment remains a standard test case in ethics classes, and in recent years it has resurfaced in a very concrete form: engineers writing the decision logic that self-driving cars use when a collision cannot be entirely avoided.

examples.hanzi: 这样做有什么是非，以后自然会知道。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò yǒu shénme shìfēi, yǐhòu zìrán huì zhīdào.
examples.english: What the rights and wrongs of doing this are will become clear later.

examples.hanzi: 他不喜欢在背后议论别人的是非。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xǐhuan zài bèihòu yìlùn biérén de shìfēi.
examples.english: He doesn't like gossiping behind people's backs.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk, as in 说, 话, 请; 诱 is to coax with words.
秀 (xiù) hints at the sound: 诱 yòu is close to 透 tòu and 锈 xiù.
饣 (food; traditional 食) — marks food and eating, as in 饭 meal, 饿 hungry; 饵 is bait or a cake.
耳 (ěr) — same sound: 饵 ěr; 耳 means ear.

example.hanzi: 渔夫在鱼钩上挂了一条虫子做诱饵。
example.pinyin: Yúfū zài yúgōu shàng guàle yì tiáo chóngzi zuò yòu'ěr.
example.english: The fisherman hung a worm on the hook as bait.
example.fact: Deep-sea anglerfish dangle a glowing lure called an esca above their mouths, its light produced by colonies of bioluminescent bacteria living symbiotically inside the tissue. In the total darkness thousands of meters down, where sunlight never reaches, the glow attracts curious prey close enough for the anglerfish to strike, a hunting strategy first described scientifically in the early 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 商家用打折作诱饵，吸引了很多顾客。
examples.pinyin: Shāngjiā yòng dǎzhé zuò yòu'ěr, xīyǐn le hěn duō gùkè.
examples.english: The store used discounts as bait to attract lots of customers.

examples.hanzi: 不要被免费的诱饵骗了。
examples.pinyin: Búyào bèi miǎnfèi de yòu'ěr piàn le.
examples.english: Don't be fooled by free bait.

meanings: (fig.) (literary) person at the height of success

components.note: 飞 (fly) — simplified from 飛, a bird with spread wings.
龙 — a picture of a dragon, simplified from 龍. It also sounds out 聋 lóng, 笼 lóng and 拢 lǒng.

example.hanzi: 传说中的飞龙能在云层间自由穿梭。
example.pinyin: Chuánshuō zhōng de fēilóng néng zài yúncéng jiān zìyóu chuānsuō.
example.english: The legendary flying dragon can move freely between the clouds.
example.fact: Quetzalcoatlus, a pterosaur that soared over what is now Texas around 70 million years ago, had a wingspan of up to 11 meters — comparable to a small airplane — making it one of the largest flying animals ever discovered. Its bones were hollow and remarkably light for its size, likely letting it launch itself into the air with a powerful leap rather than a running start.

examples.hanzi: 这个飞龙形状的风筝很大。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fēilóng xíngzhuàng de fēngzheng hěn dà.
examples.english: This dragon-shaped kite is very big.

examples.hanzi: 故事里有一条会喷火的飞龙。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ yǒu yì tiáo huì pēn huǒ de fēilóng.
examples.english: There is a fire-breathing flying dragon in the story.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — marks mountains, as in 岛, 峰; 崭 first meant steep and high, then striking and brand new, as in 崭新.
斩 (zhǎn) — same sound: 崭 zhǎn. 斩 also sounds out 暂 zàn.
斤 (axe) — chopping, as in 所, 斩: freshly cut wood is new (薪 xīn is firewood).
亲 (qīn) is a close sound clue for xīn.

example.hanzi: 他昨天买了一辆崭新的自行车。
example.pinyin: Tā zuótiān mǎile yí liàng zhǎnxīn de zìxíngchē.
example.english: He bought a brand-new bicycle yesterday.
example.fact: The distinctive 'new car smell' comes from dozens of volatile organic compounds off-gassing from plastics, adhesives, and foam inside a freshly built vehicle; researchers have identified over 50 different compounds contributing to it. Some automakers now engineer the scent deliberately, spraying specific chemical blends onto interior materials so every new car smells recognizably 'brand new.'

examples.hanzi: 搬进崭新的房子后，一家人都很高兴。
examples.pinyin: Bān jìn zhǎnxīn de fángzi hòu, yì jiā rén dōu hěn gāoxìng.
examples.english: After moving into a brand-new house, the whole family was happy.

examples.hanzi: 他穿着一身崭新的校服去上学。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yì shēn zhǎnxīn de xiàofú qù shàngxué.
examples.english: He went to school in a brand-new uniform.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
鸟 (bird) — marks birds, as in 鸡 chicken, 鹅 goose; 鹰 is the eagle or hawk.

example.hanzi: 一只老鹰在空中盘旋，寻找猎物。
example.pinyin: Yì zhī lǎoyīng zài kōngzhōng pánxuán, xúnzhǎo lièwù.
example.english: An eagle circled in the sky, searching for prey.
example.fact: The bald eagle, adopted as a national symbol of the United States in 1782, can reportedly spot a rabbit from nearly 3 kilometers away. Its eyesight is estimated to be four to eight times sharper than a human's, aided by a second, smaller fovea in each eye that is especially sensitive to movement, letting it track fast-moving prey far below while gliding at altitude.

examples.hanzi: 老鹰抓走了一只小鸡。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoyīng zhuāzǒu le yì zhī xiǎo jī.
examples.english: The eagle snatched a chick.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在玩老鹰抓小鸡的游戏。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài wán lǎoyīng zhuā xiǎo jī de yóuxì.
examples.english: The kids are playing the game of the eagle catching chicks.

components.note: 尸 (body/roof) — the top-left cover, as in 层 and 局. In 展 it works like a cover over cloth that is spread out; memory aid, shape is partly simplified.
衣 (clothing) — a bit of this sits inside 展. Dictionary story: laying out clothes to display them, hence 'unfold, exhibit' in 展示.
见 (see) — marks looking and seeing, as in 观 watch, 现 appear; 览 is looking over something, as in 展览 exhibition.

example.hanzi: 这个博物馆正在举办一场关于古代文明的展览。
example.pinyin: Zhège bówùguǎn zhèngzài jǔbàn yì chǎng guānyú gǔdài wénmíng de zhǎnlǎn.
example.english: This museum is currently holding an exhibition about ancient civilizations.
example.fact: The Great Exhibition of 1851 in London was held inside the Crystal Palace, a vast structure of iron and glass built specifically to house it. Over six million visitors attended — roughly a third of Britain's population at the time — and the exhibition's profits later helped fund the founding of the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Science Museum, and the Natural History Museum.

examples.hanzi: 这个周末有一个汽车展览，你想去看吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhōumò yǒu yí gè qìchē zhǎnlǎn, nǐ xiǎng qù kàn ma?
examples.english: There is a car show this weekend; do you want to see it?

examples.hanzi: 展览的门票是五十块。
examples.pinyin: Zhǎnlǎn de ménpiào shì wǔshí kuài.
examples.english: The exhibition ticket costs fifty yuan.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤; water means life: 活 is alive.
舌 (shé, tongue) is a loose sound clue for huó; also in 话 huà.
足 (foot, ⻊) — foot actions, as in 跑 run, 跳 jump, 路 road.
夭 (yāo) is only a loose sound clue for yuè.

example.hanzi: 退休后，他在社区里依然十分活跃。
example.pinyin: Tuìxiū hòu, tā zài shèqū lǐ yīrán shífēn huóyuè.
example.english: After retiring, he remained very active in the community.
example.fact: Yellowstone sits atop one of the most geologically active volcanic systems on Earth, its underground magma chamber occasionally causing the ground surface to rise and fall by centimeters over the course of a year. Scientists at the Yellowstone Volcano Observatory monitor this activity continuously, though the last caldera-forming eruption there occurred roughly 630,000 years ago.

examples.hanzi: 她是班上最活跃的学生。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì bān shàng zuì huóyuè de xuésheng.
examples.english: She is the most active student in the class.

examples.hanzi: 晚会上的气氛特别活跃。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnhuì shàng de qìfēn tèbié huóyuè.
examples.english: The atmosphere at the party was especially lively.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 车 is a cart or vehicle, as in 轮, 输, 车; 转 is turning of wheels.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 转 is zhuǎn; 专 also sounds out 传 chuán and 砖 zhuān.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 说 say, 问 ask; 告 is "to tell". 告 also gives sound to 造 zào and 靠 kào.

example.hanzi: 请你转告他，会议改到明天下午。
example.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ zhuǎngào tā, huìyì gǎidào míngtiān xiàwǔ.
example.english: Please tell him that the meeting has been moved to tomorrow afternoon.
example.fact: Long before telegraphs, the Persian Empire under Darius I built the Angarium around 500 BC, a relay system of mounted riders stationed at intervals along royal roads who passed messages horse to horse. The Greek historian Herodotus wrote that it could carry news roughly ten times faster than a single traveler riding the whole distance alone.

examples.hanzi: 请你转告大家，明天不用来了。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ zhuǎngào dàjiā, míngtiān búyòng lái le.
examples.english: Please tell everyone that they don't need to come tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 我会把你的话转告给经理。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì bǎ nǐ de huà zhuǎngào gěi jīnglǐ.
examples.english: I will pass your words on to the manager.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 这项政策深得人心。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè shēn dé rénxīn.
example.english: This policy has won broad public support.
example.fact: French sociologist Gustave Le Bon argued in his 1895 book The Crowd that individuals lose their sense of personal responsibility once absorbed into a crowd, becoming swept up in shared emotion rather than independent judgment. The book influenced decades of later research into collective behavior and public opinion, and it shaped how 20th-century propagandists thought about swaying mass sentiment.

examples.hanzi: 这样做会失去人心。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò huì shīqù rénxīn.
examples.english: Doing this will lose people's trust.

examples.hanzi: 人心都是肉长的，他会理解你的。
examples.pinyin: Rénxīn dōu shì ròu zhǎng de, tā huì lǐjiě nǐ de.
examples.english: People have hearts of flesh; he will understand you.

meanings: to borrow sth for another use
to borrow an idea for one's own use

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 借 is a deal between people, as in 借口.
昔 (xī) — near sound — 借 is jiè; 昔 also sounds out 惜 xī and 错 cuò.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 我可以借用一下你的充电器吗？
example.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ jièyòng yíxià nǐ de chōngdiànqì ma?
example.english: Can I borrow your charger for a bit?
example.fact: The Library of Alexandria, founded in Egypt around the 3rd century BC, reportedly required ships arriving in port to hand over any scrolls on board so scribes could copy them before returning the originals to their owners. This one-sided borrowing scheme helped the library grow into what is often described as the ancient world's largest collection of written knowledge.

examples.hanzi: 这个词是从英语借用来的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cí shì cóng Yīngyǔ jièyòng lái de.
examples.english: This word was borrowed from English.

examples.hanzi: 你能借用我的伞吗？外面在下雨。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng jièyòng wǒ de sǎn ma? Wàimiàn zài xià yǔ.
examples.english: Can you borrow my umbrella? It's raining outside.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 莓 is a berry plant, as in 草 grass, 花 flower.
每 (měi) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.

example.hanzi: 我喜欢吃草莓。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī cǎoméi.
example.english: I like eating strawberries.
example.fact: 莓 is bound: 草莓 (strawberry), 蓝莓 (blueberry), 树莓 (raspberry).

examples.hanzi: 我早上吃了一碗蓝莓。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang chī le yì wǎn lánméi.
examples.english: This morning I ate a bowl of blueberries.

examples.hanzi: 这个蛋糕上有很多草莓。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dàngāo shàng yǒu hěn duō cǎoméi.
examples.english: There are many strawberries on this cake.

components.note: 亦 is an old picture of a person (大) with two dots marking the armpits — the original word for armpit. 'Also' is a sound borrowing; 腋 yè later took over armpit.
亠 (lid) — the visible top. Sound clue: 亦 is the sound part of 弈 yì chess, 奕 yì, 迹 jì trace.

example.hanzi: 他是我的老师，亦是我的朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de lǎoshī, yì shì wǒ de péngyou.
example.english: He is my teacher and also my friend.
example.fact: 亦 is literary for 也. In 亦师亦友 ('both teacher and friend') it forms a handy pattern. 不亦乐乎 ('isn't that a joy?') is now also used to mean 'extremely', as in 忙得不亦乐乎.

examples.hanzi: 这位医生亦是一位作家。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yīshēng yì shì yí wèi zuòjiā.
examples.english: This doctor is also a writer.

examples.hanzi: 此事亦非他的责任。
examples.pinyin: Cǐ shì yì fēi tā de zérèn.
examples.english: This matter is also not his responsibility.

components.note: 夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.
聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.

example.hanzi: 教室里传来一阵阵笑声。
example.pinyin: Jiàoshì lǐ chuánlái yí zhènzhèn xiàoshēng.
example.english: Bursts of laughter came from the classroom.
example.fact: The distinctive 'laughing' call of the spotted hyena is not amusement at all — biologists studying hyena clans in the Serengeti found it is actually a vocalization used to signal submission and social rank during competitive feeding, produced most often by lower-ranking animals being pushed away from a kill.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝的笑声让全家人都开心。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao de xiàoshēng ràng quán jiā rén dōu kāixīn.
examples.english: The baby's laughter makes the whole family happy.

examples.hanzi: 操场上传来孩子们的笑声。
examples.pinyin: Cāochǎng shàng chuánlái háizimen de xiàoshēng.
examples.english: The sound of children's laughter drifts from the playground.

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
雨 (rain) — a picture of drops falling from the sky 一 through a cloud. As radical it marks weather, as in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder, 雾 fog.

example.hanzi: 外面开始下雨了，你带伞了吗？
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn kāishǐ xiàyǔ le, nǐ dài sǎn le ma?
example.english: It's starting to rain outside, did you bring an umbrella?
example.fact: Venus is covered in clouds of sulfuric acid, and it technically does rain there — but the droplets evaporate in the intense heat long before they can reach the scorching 465°C surface. This kind of evaporating rainfall, called virga, also happens far less dramatically on Earth over hot deserts.

examples.hanzi: 明天可能会下雨，记得带伞。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān kěnéng huì xià yǔ, jìde dài sǎn.
examples.english: It might rain tomorrow, so remember your umbrella.

examples.hanzi: 下雨天我喜欢待在家里看书。
examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ tiān wǒ xǐhuan dāi zài jiā lǐ kàn shū.
examples.english: On rainy days I like staying at home reading.

components.note: 尸 (body) — marks the body and its posture; 履 is the body walking on shoes, then to tread and carry out, as in 履行.
復 (fù, return) — repeated steps going back and forth, so 履 is shoes worn by walkers, hence to tread or fulfil.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 双方必须履行合同中规定的义务。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng bìxū lǚxíng hétong zhōng guīdìng de yìwù.
example.english: Both parties must fulfill the obligations specified in the contract.
example.fact: The 1648 Peace of Westphalia, a set of treaties ending the Thirty Years' War, is often cited as the origin of the modern expectation that states fulfill their treaty obligations and respect one another's sovereign borders. That principle, sometimes called the Westphalian system, still underlies much of international law today.

examples.hanzi: 他必须履行自己的诺言。
examples.pinyin: Tā bìxū lǚxíng zìjǐ de nuòyán.
examples.english: He must keep his promise.

examples.hanzi: 公司有责任履行对客户的承诺。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yǒu zérèn lǚxíng duì kèhù de chéngnuò.
examples.english: The company has a responsibility to fulfill its commitments to customers.

components.note: 九 — originally a bent arm (elbow), later borrowed to write nine. 九 also sounds out 究 jiū and 鸠 jiū.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 电影九点开始，我们八点半出发吧。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ, wǒmen bā diǎn bàn chūfā ba.
example.english: The movie starts at nine o'clock, let's leave at eight thirty.
example.fact: Mechanical clock towers spread across European cities starting in the 14th century, and several, including the famous astronomical clock in Prague, added dials tracking not just the hour but the positions of the sun, moon, and zodiac constellations. For centuries these towers doubled as the most sophisticated public science instruments many townspeople would ever see.

examples.hanzi: 明天早上九点我们在门口见。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān zǎoshang jiǔ diǎn wǒmen zài ménkǒu jiàn.
examples.english: We'll meet at the door at nine tomorrow morning.

examples.hanzi: 现在是九点一刻，快要迟到了。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài shì jiǔ diǎn yí kè, kuàiyào chídào le.
examples.english: It's nine fifteen now and we're about to be late.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
玉 (jade) — jade kept under a roof: treasure. The traditional 寶 also had 贝 (cowrie, money).
石 (stone) — a rock 口 at the foot of a cliff 厂; as a radical it marks stones and minerals, as in 破, 码, 砖, 磨.

example.hanzi: 这枚戒指上镶着一颗蓝色的宝石。
example.pinyin: Zhè méi jièzhi shàng xiāngzhe yì kē lánsè de bǎoshí.
example.english: This ring is set with a blue gemstone.
example.fact: The Hope Diamond, a 45.52-carat blue stone now held at the Smithsonian, is believed to have formed roughly a billion years ago at a depth of at least 660 kilometers below Earth's surface — far deeper than most diamonds, which typically form 150 to 200 kilometers down. Its blue color comes from trace amounts of boron replacing carbon atoms in its crystal structure.

examples.hanzi: 这颗宝石是爷爷留下来的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kē bǎoshí shì yéye liú xiàlái de.
examples.english: This gem was left by Grandpa.

examples.hanzi: 她的耳环上有一颗红宝石。
examples.pinyin: Tā de ěrhuán shàng yǒu yì kē hóng bǎoshí.
examples.english: Her earring has a ruby on it.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water, as in 海 sea, 河 river; 湾 is a bay, where water curves in.
弯 (wān) — same sound and also means curved: 湾 is a curve in the coast.

example.hanzi: 这个海湾风景优美，是著名的旅游胜地。
example.pinyin: Zhège hǎiwān fēngjǐng yōuměi, shì zhùmíng de lǚyóu shèngdì.
example.english: This bay has beautiful scenery and is a famous tourist destination.
example.fact: The Bay of Fundy, between Canada's Nova Scotia and New Brunswick, has the largest tidal range on Earth, with water levels rising and falling by up to 16 meters between low and high tide. Its funnel-like shape amplifies the natural rocking motion of the water inside it, a resonance effect similar to sloshing water in a bathtub, but on the scale of an entire coastline.

examples.hanzi: 渔船停在平静的海湾里。
examples.pinyin: Yúchuán tíng zài píngjìng de hǎiwān lǐ.
examples.english: The fishing boats are anchored in the calm bay.

examples.hanzi: 这个海湾的水很清，可以游泳。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hǎiwān de shuǐ hěn qīng, kěyǐ yóuyǒng.
examples.english: The water in this bay is clear and you can swim.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and prayer: 神, 福, 祝; 祈 is to pray.
斤 (jīn) is only a loose sound clue for qí.
求 (seek) — the original picture of a fur coat (裘 qiú adds 衣); "seek, request" is a borrowed use. 求 sounds out 球 qiú and 救 jiù.

example.hanzi: 人们在庙里祈求平安。
example.pinyin: Rénmen zài miào lǐ qíqiú píng'ān.
example.english: People pray at the temple for peace and safety.
example.fact: Archaeologists have recovered votive offerings — small clay figurines, coins, and inscribed tablets left by worshippers asking for health or good fortune — at temple sites more than 3,000 years old, including at the Temple of Amun in Karnak, Egypt. The practice of leaving a physical token of a prayer behind is one of the oldest continuously documented human rituals.

examples.hanzi: 她祈求上天保佑家人平安。
examples.pinyin: Tā qíqiú shàngtiān bǎoyòu jiārén píng'ān.
examples.english: She prayed that heaven would protect her family.

examples.hanzi: 他祈求大家的原谅。
examples.pinyin: Tā qíqiú dàjiā de yuánliàng.
examples.english: He begged for everyone's forgiveness.
